findings.title: Date-override slots bypass busy-time checks
findings.body: When a slot falls within a date override, this returns `true` before checking `busy`. Date overrides change a host’s working hours; they do not make existing bookings or calendar events disappear. As a result, a fixed host can be offered a slot that conflicts with a booking or calendar event during the override.

findings.title: Working-hours validation rejects valid split shifts and misses event end times
findings.body: This uses `find` to reject a slot if it is outside *any* working-hours interval on that weekday. For a host with separate morning and afternoon intervals, a slot inside the afternoon interval is rejected because it is outside the morning interval. Also, `end` is set to the slot start time, so a slot that starts within an interval but extends past its end is accepted. Fixed-host availability can therefore be incorrectly removed or offered.

findings.title: Zero-length date overrides are never detected by equality
findings.body: The two `dayjs` calls create distinct objects, so `===` is always false even when the override start and end represent the same instant. The intended zero-length-override handling is skipped; in particular, a candidate slot starting exactly at that instant can fall through to `dateOverrideExist` and be treated as available.
